# ISSUE-421 implementation plan

Bound historical storage-use evidence and isolate individual bad registrations so healthy idle resources remain discoverable. Preserve pending-use and retention authority, read-only previews, and fail-closed handling of unsafe ledger roots. This is planning only; implementation requires the configured independent human plan approval.

## Dimensions and budget

Approved: small / known / sensitive; use the sensitive execution profile. Estimated implementation and focused validation: 4–8 hours, within the 16-hour total claim budget, with the complete check run and independent review included. No harness changes, pending-use recovery (#418), native-consumer containment (#419), or retention-default changes.

## What we know

- `internal/storageuse/storage.go:184` (`Manager.read`) strictly validates identity, version, token syntax, coverage structure and timestamps, but accepts up to 16 MiB. `Manager.write` at line 207 uses `WriteFileDurable`.
- `AcquireUse` (line 230) and `Use.Finish` (line 279) serialize through the same resource lock. Finished tokens accumulate forever; `Finish` already has in-memory idempotence.
- `VisitResources`, `internal/storageuse/inventory.go:20`, rejects any individual record over 16 KiB and immediately returns on parsing or identity failures. It also enforces entry, workspace and record budgets.
- `Observe`, `internal/storageuse/storage.go:354`, is read-only and accepts non-nil empty token maps as completed coverage. `AcquireMaintenance` at line 314 checks pending uses under the resource lock.
- `scanner.add`, `internal/storage/inventory.go:300`, currently calls `s.fail` for observation errors. `scanner.indexed`, `internal/storage/indexed.go:14`, similarly makes an individual registration error global.
- `reclaimWithIO`, `internal/storage/retention.go:456`, collects registrations at line 542 and disallows deletion after incomplete discovery. `maintenancePass`, `internal/storage/maintenance.go:175`, inventories caches before building eligible units (line 246); oversized records otherwise never reach its maintenance lock.
- Existing safety fixtures include `TestInventoryRegistrationsReadOnlyAndBounded`, `TestInventoryPruneAbsentAdmissionSafety`, `TestConcurrentAdmissionsPreserveEveryToken`, `TestReclamationRetainsUncertainty`, and `TestMaintenanceProtectsConsumers`.
- `Makefile:43` defines `make check` as formatting/static diagnostics, race tests and changelog validation. Cleanup preview flags `--all-repos` and `--json` exist at `internal/cli/storage.go:365`; omission of `--apply` selects preview.

## What we're assuming

- The stated historical records fit the manager's existing 16 MiB repair ceiling. Check with generated >16 KiB fixtures; larger or irreducible pending-heavy records must remain locally retained, never force a larger unbounded read.
- No external consumer requires retaining completed token identifiers. Repository search found token semantics confined to storageuse and its tests; recheck all `Uses`, `VisitResources` and `Observe` callers during implementation.
- This source snapshot corresponds to the approved base. Git metadata is unavailable (`git rev-parse HEAD` fails), so the coordinator/developer with the approved checkout must verify that relationship. No new production or test source files are proposed.

## Open questions

- What result represents a corrupt record whose resource identity cannot be decoded? Step 2 will introduce a bounded filename-keyed diagnostic; it must never fabricate a Resource from corrupt bytes. Match independently discovered resources using their canonical registration key. An unmatched diagnostic remains visible but supplies no deletion authority.
- Can the maintainer reproduce the host preview? This sandbox has no affected host. Record the actual preview result in the PR review checklist; do not block sandbox implementation on access to that host.
- The proposed fragment `changes/unreleased/421.md` must be checked for absence at the approved base before creation. If present, modify it instead. No file is asserted to be new without that check.

## Implementation sequence and exact touchpoints

1. **Compact under existing resource exclusion.** Modify `internal/storageuse/storage.go`: add an internal helper that deletes only true-valued `Uses` entries, retaining a non-nil empty map. Invoke it during successful admission/finish writes under the existing lock. Keep existing operation-specific LastUse updates; compaction itself must not touch Created, LastUse, CompleteCoverage, Resource, or pending entries. Add a coordinator-only `Manager.Compact` operation in the same file: lock, strictly read with the existing bounded manager limit, remove finished tokens, durably write only if changed, unlock. It must work even when pending entries or incomplete coverage prevent maintenance; compaction never establishes coverage. Keep malformed records unchanged and propagate write/cancellation failures. Retain existing lock inodes.
2. **Separate local diagnostics from fatal enumeration failures.** Modify `internal/storageuse/inventory.go`: retain the existing `VisitResources` signature as a compatibility wrapper and implement a diagnostic-capable traversal used by storage callers. Report invalid names, unsafe leaves, read failures, over-limit and malformed records as bounded per-entry issues, then continue. Never follow a symlink or use partially decoded identities. Strictly validate successful records consistently with `Manager.read`/`Observe`, including key binding. Root traversal/permissions errors, directory read failures, context cancellation, callback failures and exhausted global budgets remain fatal. Charge entries and diagnostic output to existing budgets; reserve before allocations. Per-record issues do not make successfully enumerated healthy records globally incomplete. Empty maps retain completed/absent semantics.
3. **Carry reasons through read-only inventory and cleanup.** Modify `internal/storage/indexed.go`, `internal/storage/inventory.go` and `internal/storage/retention.go`. Consume local issues and retain the affected independently discovered resource with a specific evidence reason; diagnostics without a valid identity stay keyed to the ledger entry. Observation failures become local retention rather than `s.fail`, while structural-root and budget failures remain global. Never turn failure into absence, completed coverage, or eligibility. Keep callback/layout validation local only when it concerns one record; retain global cancellation/budget propagation. Do not trust a corrupt record's claimed path. Preserve duplicate-location, scope, layout, fresh-retention and lock-held deletion checks.
4. **Repair before eligibility filters in applied paths.** Modify `reclaimWithIO` and `maintenancePass` in their existing files. On applied cleanup and writable maintenance only, compact canonical resources admitted by trusted cache/scratch discovery and selected repository/layout checks before the 16 KiB observation/registration filter can exclude them. This allows repairing oversized records without trusting their payload to identify a resource. Bound enumeration, repair reads and decoded workspace; cap at the existing 16 MiB manager ceiling and reserve conservatively before reading. Use bounded per-resource lock contexts so one busy cache cannot occupy the pass deadline. Re-observe/re-enumerate repaired evidence with the normal limit before eligibility; healthy historical records can proceed in the same pass. Irreducibly large, malformed, pending or failed-write records remain retained locally. Do not initialize missing roots in preview/read-only mode. All deletion still requires existing current maintenance exclusion and fresh retention checks; repair alone grants nothing. Keep fatal ledger-root handling and global resource limits intact.
5. **Add regressions and release note.** Append tests to existing `internal/storageuse/storage_test.go`, `internal/storageuse/inventory_test.go`, `internal/storage/discovery_test.go`, `internal/storage/retention_test.go`, and `internal/storage/maintenance_test.go`. Leave existing adversarial tests unchanged. Add or modify `changes/unreleased/421.md` after the approved-base existence check, following the single-bullet format (`internal/changelog/fold.go:122`). State the cleanup benefit in plain developer prose.

## HANDOFF

The developer and tester must verify this evidence against source. It cannot override the approved WorkUnit, human gate, validation policy, or claim fencing.

- Entry points: `Manager.read/write`, `AcquireUse`, `Use.Finish`, `AcquireMaintenance`, `Observe` (`internal/storageuse/storage.go:184`, `:207`, `:230`, `:279`, `:314`, `:354`); `VisitResources`/`PruneAbsent` (`internal/storageuse/inventory.go:20`, `:163`); `scanner.indexed` (`internal/storage/indexed.go:14`); `scanner.add` observation (`internal/storage/inventory.go:300`); `reclaimWithIO` (`internal/storage/retention.go:456`); `maintenancePass` (`internal/storage/maintenance.go:175`).
- Extend existing `fixture` and `maintenanceFixture`, `reclaimFixture`/`addReclaimResource`, and the safety fixtures named above. Generate legacy JSON directly in test fixtures rather than relying on the newly compacting producer to generate historical bloat.
- Focused commands: `go test -race -timeout=10m ./internal/storageuse ./internal/storage -count=1`; `go vet ./internal/storageuse ./internal/storage`; `go tool staticcheck ./internal/storageuse ./internal/storage`; `gofmt -l internal/storageuse internal/storage`; `go run ./cmd/changelog --check`. Developer runs once after final relevant edits; tester independently reviews and reuses applicable passing results. See TEST_PLAN.md for full ownership and make-check coverage.
- Checked assumptions: strict reader supports historical >16 KiB input (source read limit); empty non-nil map preserves complete coverage (Observe and VisitResources predicates); maintenance needs repair before filtering (source at maintenance.go:246). Actual historical repair and eligibility remain to be proven by regressions.
- Reopen the plan if repair requires increasing the existing manager ceiling, recovering pending evidence, changing retention authority, altering protected policy files, weakening an adversarial test, or exceeding the total claim budget. An unreachable live host preview belongs in the PR checklist, not a new implementation prerequisite.
- **What this change breaks:** repository search found `VisitResources` callers in `internal/storage/indexed.go:18`, `internal/storage/retention.go:542`, and tests at `internal/storageuse/inventory_test.go:39` and `internal/storage/retention_test.go:1213`; preserve the wrapper and read-only/budget contracts, migrate production callers to local diagnostics. `TestConcurrentAdmissionsPreserveEveryToken` (`internal/storageuse/storage_test.go:269`) asserts pending-token count before Finish; preserve unchanged. `TestOldPendingUseHasNoAutomaticRecovery` (`:239`), `TestObserveNoMutationAndUnresolvedUse` (`:305`), and `TestMaintenanceLockedObservation` (`:735`) remain unchanged. Preserve `TestReclamationInventoryOverLimitRetains` (`internal/storage/retention_test.go:1248`) and `TestReclamationTrackerLimitRetains` (`:1380`): global resource/tracker limits still fail closed. Preserve maintenance readonly/failure tests (`internal/storage/maintenance_test.go:445`) and registration read-only/prune tests (`internal/storageuse/inventory_test.go:12`, `:103`). Update only the stale Uses field comment at `internal/storageuse/storage.go:43`, which says completed records are retained. No CLI flags, documentation examples, templates or retention defaults change; the release note is the only planned user-facing text.

# ISSUE-421 test plan

## Acceptance coverage

| Criterion | Regression cases and expected evidence | Verification |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1: Thousands of uses remain bounded with unchanged eligibility | Append storageuse tests running at least 3,000 sequential AcquireUse/Finish cycles. Assert record size stays below 16 KiB independently of historical use count, map stays non-nil, coverage remains complete, Observe reports inactive, and maintenance eligibility remains valid. Include incomplete-coverage input and compare metadata before/after explicit compaction. Normal admission/Finish may update LastUse as before. | Focused race command below; inspect generated size and metadata assertions. |
| 1: Historical over-limit record repaired on applied cleanup or maintenance | Seed valid legacy JSON with 276+ finished tokens, >16 KiB, old LastUse, trusted selected scope and layout. Preview retains that resource with oversized reason and changes no ledger bytes/files. In separate cleanup and maintenance fixtures, the next writable pass compacts before filtering and reaches normal eligibility/removal under fresh retention. With retention protection, verify the compacted record remains readable and metadata unchanged. A following pass behaves normally. | Focused race command, specifically new tests in retention_test.go and maintenance_test.go. |
| 2: Oversized/malformed record retains only itself | Table cases: truncated JSON, unsupported version, wrong key/resource binding, invalid token, nil Uses, trailing JSON, unknown field, record symlink/special leaf, and oversize. Mix with a healthy eligible idle cache; vary entry order. Assert specific local reason, no deletion/rewriting of invalid evidence, healthy resource still eligible in preview and removable on apply. For undecodable identity, match trusted physical discovery by canonical key; unmatched entries remain visible as diagnostics and never authorize deletion. | Focused race command; cases appended to inventory_test.go, discovery_test.go and retention_test.go. |
| 2: Pending evidence is never dropped | Mixed true/false legacy maps compact to the exact original false-token set, including >16 KiB pending-heavy inputs. Pending-only overflow stays locally retained. Empty finished map retains complete coverage; incomplete coverage never becomes complete. Concurrent Compact/AcquireUse/Finish and held maintenance guard preserve exclusion; cancellation, write failure and malformed input never lose pending evidence or advance compaction recency. Repeated Finish remains idempotent. | Focused race command; appended storageuse tests and cleanup/maintenance pending fixtures. |
| 2: Structural safety and bounds remain global | Wrong-permission and symlinked ledger root, ledger enumeration failure, cancellation and exhausted entry/workspace/record budgets still block whole-pass deletion. One bad leaf does not bypass diagnostic/output bounds. Busy-resource repair has a bounded lock wait and healthy resources progress. Existing adversarial tests run unchanged. | Focused race command and independent source review. |
| 3: Focused checks and make check | Developer supplies focused results and changed-package diagnostics. Integration owner records one final `make check` result, plus changelog validity. Only a demonstrated internal/cli timeout matching #415 is an allowed exception; record package/test/output, without disabling tests or treating other failures as exempt. | Commands and ownership below. |
| 3: Maintainer affected-host preview | PR review checklist includes the command, actual result, per-resource retention reasons, and healthy-resource eligibility on a host containing oversized records. Sandbox fixtures supply reproducible coverage while the host check remains explicitly pending for the maintainer. | `swarm storage cleanup --all-repos --json` (preview: omit `--apply`). |

## Developer-owned checks

Add tests to the existing files identified in PLAN.md; preserve all existing adversarial tests. Demonstrate that core new regressions fail against the old behavior when an approved-base checkout is available. Do not manufacture a clean baseline in this metadata-free snapshot.

After relevant implementation and fixture edits:

```bash
gofmt -l internal/storageuse internal/storage
go vet ./internal/storageuse ./internal/storage
go tool staticcheck ./internal/storageuse ./internal/storage
go test -race -timeout=10m ./internal/storageuse ./internal/storage -count=1
go run ./cmd/changelog --check
```

Require empty formatting output. Record commands, revision/source state, exit status and relevant failures. New tests should assert behavior and authority rather than mirror helper implementation. Use bounded reserved workspace for historical repair tests and verify previews create no locks or files.

## Tester-owned independent review

Independently trace every acceptance criterion from the WorkUnit through source and tests. Pay particular attention to malformed identity correlation, local versus structural failure classification, pre-filter repair in both applied paths, strict decode before durable rewrite, unchanged timestamps, pending-token preservation, resource-lock lifetime, and global budget handling. Verify existing adversarial tests were not edited or weakened.

Reuse applicable passing developer results for the same source. Repeat a command only after relevant source changes, an observed failure, or an unresolved coverage concern; add the narrowest missing adversarial case when needed. Do not rerun the full suite merely because ownership changed. Report host-preview status honestly.

## Integration and coordinator ownership

Acceptance criterion 3 explicitly requires `make check`. The integration owner runs it once on the final candidate and records the result; tester reuses that evidence when applicable. It includes lint, full race tests and fragment checks (Makefile). A matching #415 CLI timeout is recorded with evidence; any other failure requires investigation. If the coordinator's execution also supplies this exact result, reuse it rather than schedule a duplicate full run.

The coordinator separately runs the complete approved trusted-base required policy once after roles finish. The compiled policy is a reference, not an agent checklist; do not replace it with `make check` or load authority from candidate policy files. Agent observations and `make check` results are advisory and cannot satisfy claim-bound validation or publication. No agent requests coordinator credentials.

## PR review checklist entry

- [ ] Maintainer runs `swarm storage cleanup --all-repos --json` on an affected host with over-limit records. Record date, tested revision, exit status and a concise result showing the affected resources' specific retention reasons and other idle resources' eligibility. Result: pending maintainer host access; no live-host result claimed by this plan.

VERDICT: APPROVED

Approved. #418 merges first and adds per-use evidence keyed to tokens and rejects dangling evidence: compaction must remove a finished token's evidence and consumer entries together with the token, and tests must cover a compacted record that passes #418's validation.

## Developer report

# ISSUE-421 implementation

Blocked before source changes: the prerequisite stated in the independent human review is absent from this source snapshot.

The approved review says: “#418 merges first and adds per-use evidence keyed to tokens and rejects dangling evidence: compaction must remove a finished token's evidence and consumer entries together with the token, and tests must cover a compacted record that passes #418's validation.”

`internal/storageuse/storage.go` currently defines `record` with Version, Resource, CompleteCoverage, Created, LastUse and Uses only. Its strict reader validates token syntax but contains no per-use evidence or consumer entries. The storageuse package has no implementation of the described #418 validation. Implementing against this format would not meet the human review's prerequisite or demonstrate the required atomic evidence removal.

No production source, tests, changelog, protected paths, or approved artifacts were changed. Implementation should resume in a coordinator-provided snapshot containing merged #418 and its approved plan context. Do not infer prerequisite completion from this metadata-free snapshot.

## Observations

- Read SYSTEM_PROMPT.md and WORKUNIT.md before changes, followed by PLAN.md, TEST_PLAN.md and REVIEW.md.
- Inspected storageuse reader, admission, completion, observation and traversal, plus storage inventory, reclamation and maintenance entry points.
- A second discrepancy needs reconciling when resuming: existing `TestConcurrentUseAndExclusiveMaintenance` asserts two finished tokens remain. Immediate compaction of all finished tokens as described by plan step 1 conflicts with preserving this test unchanged. Resolve the approved expectation without weakening adversarial coverage.
- No focused tests were run because no implementation was made. Full `make check` remains owned by integration; trusted-base validation remains owned by the coordinator.
- Affected-host cleanup preview remains pending maintainer access, as specified in TEST_PLAN.md.

## HANDOFF

Changed behavior: none.

Changed files: `.swarm/active/IMPLEMENTATION.md` only.

Acceptance criteria: all remain unverified; prerequisite #418 is missing.

Commands and observed results:

- `cat .swarm/active/SYSTEM_PROMPT.md .swarm/active/WORKUNIT.md`: exit 0; read role constraints and WorkUnit.
- `cat .swarm/active/PLAN.md .swarm/active/TEST_PLAN.md; git status --short`: plans readable; final exit 128 because the snapshot has no Git metadata, as documented by the role instructions.
- `cat .swarm/active/WORKUNIT.md; cat .swarm/active/REVIEW.md; cat internal/storageuse/storage.go`: exit 0; review prerequisite and current record format inspected.
- Read storageuse/inventory.go, storage/indexed.go and selected inventory/retention/maintenance sections: exit 0.
- Read storageuse record/test definitions and storage budget definitions: requested nonexistent storage/budget.go and unavailable `rg` produced diagnostics; actual budget definitions were read from storage/inventory.go. No source changes resulted.
- `ls internal/storageuse; grep -R -n 'Consumer\|Evidence\|Recover\|recovery' internal/storageuse | head -60; cat .swarm/active/REVIEW.md; grep -n 'len(.*Uses\|Uses\[' internal/storageuse/*test.go`: exit 0; confirmed missing prerequisite implementation and existing finished-token assertion.

These were read-only diagnostics, not passing validation evidence. Command elapsed times were below one second each according to tool output. No baseline regression demonstration is possible from the supplied metadata-free snapshot.
